audit_status.review_note: Divine procession, difficult Hebrew, Sinai, vulnerable people, war, kings, gifts, and sanctuary.

notes.title: Rider in the ʿaravot
notes.body: Hebrew ba-aravot is difficult in context and has been understood as deserts/steppes or linked poetically with cloud-rider imagery. The uncertainty should remain visible.

notes.title: Received gifts / gave gifts
notes.body: The Hebrew text says the ascending figure “received gifts among humanity.” Ephesians 4:8 cites a form saying “gave gifts to people.” The reception difference is significant and should not be harmonized away.

translation_notes: This chapter completes corpus coverage as a ChatGPT-authored draft. KJV is retained as a familiar comparison layer; a separate automated reference pass adds BSB and pointed Hebrew without replacing the restored draft.
safety_note: Ancient divine-war imagery and defeated-enemy language are not authorization for holy war, ethnic hatred, or modern violence.
source_witness_audit_flags: Compare directly with WLC/OSHB, Septuagint, Dead Sea Psalms witnesses where extant, and other textual witnesses during the global audit. Preserve poetic parallelism, superscriptions, duplicate/parallel psalms, and significant Hebrew/Greek divergences rather than harmonizing them.
